messages.subject: change to shiny:::slider between Shiny 0.8.0 and 0.8.0.99
parts:
I noticed when switching to the latest development version of Shiny, 0.8.0.99, that I seem to have lost the ability to load my own custom version of the jquery slider.

Sometimes when I use a custom css file where I change a lot of colors, it can look odd if I don't also change the color of the slider bar (the light blue that displays when selecting a range of values). In my ui.R I include something like this:

tags$head(
tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css", href="styles_black_orange.css"),
tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css", href="jquery.slider.min.css")
)

In this development version I noticed my version of jquery.slider.min.css does not seem to load any more, or maybe does but is superceded by the shiny:::slider function. I can see that this function now contains a similar line:

tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css", href="shared/slider/css/jquery.slider.min.css")

which it did not contain in shiny 0.8.0. I am not aware if it simply occurred elsewhere, or if this is related to the issue I am having, but it is the only difference I can find. Is there a way I can still load my own file?

Thanks,
Matt

Yes, they show up as the following:

<html>
<head>
  ...
  <link href="styles_black_orange.css" rel="stylesheet" type="text/css"/>
  <link href="jquery.slider.min.css" rel="stylesheet" type="text/css"/>

Even though they both load, the first still changes the entire display of my app, but that latter must be superseded somewhere. I was suspecting in shiny:::slider.

On the other hand, my only evidence of a change in behavior is that my range-selected slider bar is supposed to be orange, not light blue. (My version of jquery.slider.min.css references a different image file that has an orange bar instead of a blue one.) So I suppose it is also possible that something else has changed, such as my file is not superseded elsewhere in the code but is perhaps no longer able to "see" my app/www/img/jslider.png file. But I have other images in this directory that other components of my app can still access and display in the browser.

Matt

messages.subject: Re: change to shiny:::slider between Shiny 0.8.0 and 0.8.0.99
parts:
To solve the problem, you need to put your CSS *after* sliderInput()
to make sure your CSS overrides the default style, e.g.

shinyUI(basicPage(
sliderInput('foo','Foo', 0, 10, c(1, 5)),

tags$head(
tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css",
href="styles_black_orange.css"),
tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css", href="jquery.slider.min.css")
)

))


Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: change to shiny:::slider between Shiny 0.8.0 and 0.8.0.99
parts:
Hi Yihui,

Thanks so much. This works. At first I thought you might have meant it was simply a matter of load order and I could put these tags at the bottom of sidebarPanel(), in the event I have multiple sliders and don't want to duplicate code. But unless I did it wrong, it does appear that it only loads my slider if I immediately follow the sliderInput call with the css reference.

The other thing I noticed, since I tend to use uiOutput() in conjunction with renderUI() much of the time, is that this only works when sliderInput() is explicitly referenced in ui.R. Fortunately, on t he server side, I was able to achieve the same result with something like the following:

output$Yrs <- renderUI({
if(!is.null(yrs())){
div(
sliderInput("yrs","",yrs()[1],tail(yrs(),1),range(yrs()),step=1,format="#"),
tags$head(tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css", href="jquery.slider.min.css"))
)
}
})

If I have multiple sliders in an app, as well as employing code externalization (with file sourcing) so that for large complex apps not all code is crammed into one or two files, it is not ideal to have this hardcoded in various places. However, at least it works again and does allow me to have a custom slider.

Thanks,
Matt
